subject (6b6d05a08) and this one's (596cb6e50), +6,904/-1,947 over 46 files in
src/frontend/gpui/ alone, aimed squarely at the findings below. Every reading
taken before them is stale by construction. This file re-takes them.

and every claim names the commit it was measured against, in the same sentence.

live macOS GUI session and a kTCCServiceScreenCapture grant. A gate that cannot

prerequisitesRepairedBeforeAnythingCould.measured: `git submodule status` printed `-a0f1df6a6512340df9ababe59f55140c94a2200f libs/nim-regex`. `just build-gpui` died with `src/frontend/viewmodel/host/text_match.nim(66, 8) Error: cannot open file: regex`, and `just build-once`'s own preflight named the cause exactly: `MISSING 1 uninitialised submodule(s)`. config.nims line 31 adds `libs/nim-regex/src` to the path; the submodule arrived with 2097ae648 (Find in Files).
prerequisitesRepairedBeforeAnythingCould.repair: `git submodule update --init libs/nim-regex`, exit 0, checked out a0f1df6a (v0.27.0). No other submodule was uninitialised.
prerequisitesRepairedBeforeAnythingCould.worthKnowing: A workspace sync that does not run `git submodule update --init` leaves every checkout one commit behind a build that cannot start. The dev shell's `.envrc` does run it; a scripted sync may not.

prerequisitesRepairedBeforeAnythingCould.what: isonim-gpui's staged PLAT-37 shims were TWO COMMITS STALE, over exactly the surface this campaign measures.
prerequisitesRepairedBeforeAnythingCould.measured: `rust/target/plat37/libgpui_nim_shim.*.dylib` were dated 2026-10-16T12:35–12:37, while isonim-gpui HEAD 0317536 is dated 2026-10-17T05:04. The two commits in between are `6b7ce61` (register font files, draw line-height) and `0317536` (per-corner radii, per-side margins, Chromium's text antialiasing) — font metrics and antialiasing, i.e. the row pitch and glyph rendering that PARITY-S5 and PARITY-P1 are about.
prerequisitesRepairedBeforeAnythingCould.repair: `nix develop --command just plat37-shims` in isonim-gpui, exit 0. Positive control that it really rebuilt: the windowed shim went 66,439,976 -> 66,770,072 bytes and the featureless one 1,595,192 -> 1,640,200.
prerequisitesRepairedBeforeAnythingCould.andTheGateCannotSeeThis: `ci/lib/build-freshness.sh` says so itself at lines 114-116: link-time inputs that are not Nim modules — 'the isonim-gpui cdylib above all' — are OUTSIDE the GPUI input digest. So `build-freshness.sh assert` would have returned 0 over a stale shim. The gate is not wrong; it is scoped, and the scope has to be covered by hand.

electronArm.deviationDeclared: SCOPING THE ELECTRON BUILD IS A DEVIATION FROM `just build-once` WITH NO ARGUMENTS, and it is flagged as one. `CODETRACER_REPROBUILD_TARGET` is build-once.sh's own documented knob (scripts/build-once.sh:466) and the Electron stamp's closure provably excludes both failing actions (`bf_electron_write_stamp` anchors to bin/ct and folds in ui.js and index.js only). The stamp was written by the real build path, not by hand.
electronArm.threeEnvironmentVariablesWithoutWhichITD: The first attempt omitted them and died with `could not provision the Nim compiler that compiles the recipe … package "nim@2.2.10" has no tarball realization for aarch64-macos`. That is reprobuild's OWN printed remedy being followed, not a workaround around it: `reprobuild does not fall back to PATH by itself`. The 2026-10-16 pass used the same three.

theBuildStampNAMESTHEWRONGBINARY.observed: The stamp reads `built_by=repro 0.1.3 (compiles with its own tool-store nim, not the nim on PATH)` although the build was driven by the local 0.2.5.
theBuildStampNAMESTHEWRONGBINARY.mechanismMeasuredThisPass: `tup` IS NOT IN THE CODETRACER DEV SHELL ON aarch64-darwin. Measured directly: inside `nix develop`, `command -v tup` is empty while `command -v nim` resolves. scripts/build-once.sh:45 therefore fires its guard and sources `.direnv/flake-profile-cf2df07c….rc` — dated 2026-08-27 — which prepends `/nix/store/fi801q3ikr5b5amalxyi2rm8xa83r894-reprobuild-0.1.3/bin`. After that source, `command -v repro` resolves to 0.1.3; before it, to the local 0.2.5. Reproduced on demand in a standalone probe.
theBuildStampNAMESTHEWRONGBINARY.whyTheBUILDwasSTILLthelocal0_2_5: build-once.sh:193 resolves the engine from the SIBLING checkout's `build/bin/` BEFORE falling back to PATH, so `$repro_bin` is …/reprobuild/build/bin/repro whatever the profile does. Confirmed by the running process — `…/fix-pxor-issues/reprobuild/build/bin/reprobuild build . --tool-provisioning=nix` — and by the ct native edge building clean, which the 0.1.3 image cannot do because it has no `dsymutil` selector.
theBuildStampNAMESTHEWRONGBINARY.soTheDEFECTisNARROW: `bf_electron_write_stamp` (ci/lib/build-freshness.sh:583) composes BF_BUILDER from `repro --version` off the ambient PATH instead of from the `$repro_bin` build-once already resolved. The stamp's provenance line is wrong; the stamp's `input_digest` and `artefact_sha256` — the only fields the gate compares — are unaffected, so no measurement in this file rests on it.
theBuildStampNAMESTHEWRONGBINARY.whatIdidAboutTheStaleDirenvProfile: NOTHING, deliberately. Deleting `.direnv/flake-profile*` is a derived-cache deletion and would be safe for `nim`, but it is also what supplies `tup` to this build path, and removing it mid-pass would have changed the build environment between my run and the 2026-10-16 run I am comparing against. The contamination is confined to one provenance string. Recorded as an unfiled issue below.

electron.command: nix develop --command env REPLAY_SERVER_BIN=<…> bash ci/test/plat37-macos-electron-capture.sh
electron.playwright: 2 passed, 4 failed (6.4m). All four failures are the same assertion at plat37-electron-window-capture.spec.ts:862, `the editor drew no rows`, which counts `div[id^='editorComponent'] .monaco-editor .view-lines .view-line` in the live DOM AFTER the window has been captured and recorded.
electron.whyExit1: The four census refusals are PARITY-S1 (below). Geometry was honoured on all six and `satisfiesG1` is true on all six.
electron.theSpecFAILSoNtheEDITORwhileTHEframeSHOW: In 3 of the 4 failures the captured frame DOES hold a drawn editor: the screen oracle located an `editor` pane in editor/state/calltrace and read highlightedLineNumber 44 and 110 in two of them, and every route record is settled and correct (busy=false; final lines 110/44/44/113/1/56, each matching its pin). So for those three the spec's DOM locator and the frame disagree, and this pass did not establish which is right. In the fourth — entry-shell — the frame genuinely has no editor: see PARITY-S14.

titleBarCropReDerived.why: Every extent comparison in the previous readings rests on a 58-device-pixel crop. `d61a918ab` (the top bar is the window's title bar, and the window is a normal desktop window) landed between those readings and this tree, so the constant could not be inherited.
titleBarCropReDerived.answer: 58 DEVICE PIXELS = 29 POINTS at scale 2.0. UNCHANGED at 596cb6e50.
derivedThreeIndependentWays: 1. THE ATTESTATION. The GPUI lane asks for a 900-point content height at `laptop`; CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo reports a 1440x929-point frame in all three laptop scenarios. 929 - 900 = 29 points = 58 device pixels.

2. THE OTHER RENDERER'S EXTENT. Electron asks for the same 1440x900, its attested frame IS 1440x900 (its spec asserts frame == getContentSize() live, which is what entitles it to --title-bar-points=0), and it captures 2880x1800. GPUI captures 2880x1858. 1858 - 1800 = 58.

3. THE PIXELS. Walking the modal gray level down the first 80 device rows of a GPUI capture: rows 0-1 are 246/240, rows 2-55 are 234 — the macOS server-drawn title bar — and the first row with a dark mode is 56. The remaining 2 device rows are the bar's dark bottom separator, giving 58. The same walk on an Electron capture finds a dark mode (27) at row 0: no title bar at all.
titleBarCropReDerived.whyD61a918abDidNotMoveIt: Its own message says so: 'Where the platform draws the frame (KDE, sway's default, macOS, Windows) the bar shows no buttons and its empty space does nothing, as before.' The client-decoration path it adds is the GNOME/Wayland one. The macOS window is still a standard titled NSWindow.
titleBarCropReDerived.controlOnTheCROP: compare.sh was given CROP_PX=0 first: it refused with `extent mismatch: gpui 2880x1858 (cropped 2880x1858) vs electron 2880x1800` and compared nothing. The harness cannot silently resample two different extents, and the refusal path is live.
titleBarCropReDerived.changeMadeToTheHARNESS: compare.sh no longer has a DEFAULT crop. The caller must pass the band it measured. A constant carried across d61a918ab is a constant nobody re-measured.

instrumentControls.flipIdentity: A frame against itself (shift 0 px) reads mean 0.0000, p90 0.0000, max 0.0000, fracOver0_10 0.0000. The differ is not reading noise.
instrumentControls.flipSizeRefusal: flipdiff exits 3 on any extent mismatch; compare.sh refuses before reaching it. Exercised this pass with CROP_PX=0.
instrumentControls.flipdiffProvenance: REUSED the binary built 2026-10-12 at build/plat37-parity/flipdiff rather than rebuilt, and compiled OUTSIDE the dev shell was never needed as a result. Justified: it was built from codetracer-image-diff ee9fb397b and that repo is STILL at ee9fb397b today, so the FLIP implementation is byte-identical. A fresh `nim c` of it inside the dev shell FAILED (`invalid argument '-std=c++17' not allowed with 'C'`) because image_diff adds -std=c++17 through {.passC.}; `nim cpp` is the right spelling (codetracer-image-diff/Justfile:9), and a retry was abandoned when that dev-shell entry began rebuilding Noir from source. Stated as a deviation.
instrumentControls.paneAndRowProbe: ci-side probe build/plat37-parity-2026-10-17/structdump.nim, compiled INSIDE the dev shell (exit 0). S1/S3/S5 use the EXPORTED oracle primitives unchanged — readFrame (the grader's own entry point), lineBands (ink projection, no OCR) and readGutterDigits. Readings are not uniform across frames (paneCount 4/5/7, highlightedLineNumber 1/44/56/110/113, recognised strings 80-205), so the probe is alive.
instrumentControls.chipDetectorIsAPORTandITSCONTROLFAILSONO: The inline-value detector is a port of plat42_window_record.nim's private `chipsOf` (constants ChipGround 27, EyeGround 51, GroundTolerance 3, MinChipPx 12) because that proc is not exported. Its negative control — the same detector over the fileTree pane, which cannot hold an inline value — HOLDS on every Electron frame (0 found) and FAILS on every GPUI frame (exactly 2 found). So GPUI's chip counts below are an UPPER BOUND carrying about two false positives per frame, and Electron's are clean. This is stated rather than smoothed over; it does not change S4's verdict, because the finding under test was 'at most one'.
instrumentControls.rowPitchInstrumentHADTOBECHANGEDMIDPASS: The first pitch estimator took the median centre delta only between bands whose gutter numbers differ by exactly 1 — plat42's own rule. It reads 15-22 usable steps per GPUI frame and 0-2 per Electron frame, with slips like a first line of `3738` and `1870`: the oracle's gutter grammar is far weaker on Electron frames, which PARITY-O1 already records. An estimator that good on one side and blind on the other cannot compare them. The figures reported are therefore the MODE of all consecutive lineBands centre deltas at 0.5-point resolution, which uses no OCR at all and has 6-17 supporting deltas on both sides.
instrumentControls.pixelShiftLadder: Re-measured this pass on this pass's own Electron `state` frame (2880x1800), so it is directly comparable with the P1 readings beside it.

regrade.whatEACHreportCORRESPONDStoPHYSICALLY: Both are the window's OWN surface, not a crop of the screen: the capture goes through SCContentFilter(desktopIndependentWindow:) and `satisfiesG1` is true on all thirteen frames, meaning ScreenCaptureKit handed back the same window id CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo attested. A macOS window is NOT clipped to its display in its backing store, so a 1920-point-wide window on a 1728-point display is a real 1920x1080-point surface of which 192 points are never visible, and 3840x2160 device pixels of it are real pixels the compositor rendered.
regrade.soTheCORRECTIONisCONFIRMED: The prior claim that 'no window can exceed its display, therefore Electron must be reporting a logical framebuffer' is WRONG and is withdrawn here on measurement. Electron obtains the oversized window; GPUI does not, because AppKit's default constrainFrameRect:toScreen: clamps it and isonim-gpui's build_window_class never overrides it.
regrade.contentLossHalfNOTreMEASURED: The half that matters — whether GPUI's Call Trace rows are cut mid-glyph by the window edge — was attempted and the probe FAILED ITS OWN CONTROL. Counting rows with ink in the last 6 device columns of the calltrace pane reads 0.970-0.976 for EVERY pane that reaches the window's right edge and 0.55-0.57 for every interior pane — and it reads the same 0.970 for ELECTRON's calltrace when that pane reaches the window edge too (editorWithMark 0.9704, eventLog 0.9769) as for GPUI's (0.9705, 0.9763). A reading that is identical on both sides and near-1 wherever a pane touches the edge is measuring a border, not a clipped glyph. Reported as not measured rather than as a null result.

doesTheUpstreamPLAT35LANESUPERSEDETHEPLA.verdict: NO — COMPLEMENTARY. Neither can run where the other does, and they answer different questions. Keep both; do not restructure them in this pass, as instructed.
doesTheUpstreamPLAT35LANESUPERSEDETHEPLA.platform: ci/test/plat35-gpui-window-capture.sh is Linux/Wayland only: plat35_gpui_window_capture.nim imports gui_assert/desktop_env/sway and builds `newSwayTarget(2560, 1440, …)`; the shell builds `${target}/debug/libgpui_nim_shim.so` (an ELF name), propagates LD_LIBRARY_PATH, sets ISONIM_GPUI_DECORATIONS=client and shells out to `nix shell nixpkgs#imagemagick` per frame. ci/test/plat37-macos-window-capture.sh refuses outright off Darwin (lines 182-186) and drives ScreenCaptureKit and the Quartz window server. On aarch64-darwin there is no sway, no grim and no `.so`.
doesTheUpstreamPLAT35LANESUPERSEDETHEPLA.evidenceClass: The PLAT-35 window lane writes NO JSON RECORD AT ALL — its outputs are <view>.ppm, <view>.run.log and an ImageMagick <view>.png, and it reports failure as a list of view names. It enforces exact geometry in-process as a wait predicate and never writes the fact down. The PLAT-37 pair is the only thing in the tree entitled to `satisfiesG1: true` and carries windowFramePoints, titleBarPoints, windowContentHeightPoints, viewportHonoured, viewportDeviationPoints, capturedPixels, capturedPoints, pointPixelScale and `standing: HOST-CONDITIONAL EVIDENCE` per frame. Everything measured in this file comes from fields PLAT-35's lane does not produce.
doesTheUpstreamPLAT35LANESUPERSEDETHEPLA.shouldMINEdelegateTOciLIBgpuiWindowCaptu: NO. ci/lib/gpui-window-capture.sh factors out window driving plus a settle-polled capture plus a one-line manifest; its capture primitive is `grim`, which does not exist on Darwin, it captures the SCREEN rather than the window surface, and its manifest carries no window id, bounds or scale — so satisfiesG1, windowFramePoints and titleBarPoints would have no source. Its consumers are plat40-panes-window.sh and plat41-panes-window.sh; the PLAT-35 window lane does not use it either.
doesTheUpstreamPLAT35LANESUPERSEDETHEPLA.didUpstreamsLayoutFIXresolveTHEpaneCENSU: NO. 9268c8ab3's `noUserLayout` is set in visual-alignment-capture.spec.ts (test.use at line ~888). The PLAT-37 Electron spec already had the same fixture option from 9226bc5ed, dated 2026-10-15T16:40 — before the pass that measured 7 panes. The census still refuses 4 of 6.
doesTheUpstreamPLAT35LANESUPERSEDETHEPLA.theONErealDUPLICATION: Both families now request the shared default layout by the same fixture option but run two different specs into two different output trees (src/tests/visual/captures/electron/ versus build/plat37-macos-electron). That is duplication worth collapsing later, not supersession. The one genuine divergence to reconcile is decoration semantics: PLAT-35 forces client-side decorations so the GPUI window draws its own title bar, while PLAT-37 measures a 29-point SERVER title bar and subtracts it. The two lanes are not measuring the same window chrome.

new.title: the Electron build stamp names a `repro` that did not build it, because the stale .direnv profile wins the PATH race
new.measured: At codetracer 596cb6e50 the stamp reads `built_by=repro 0.1.3` while the build ran through …/reprobuild/build/bin/reprobuild (0.2.5). `tup` is absent from the codetracer dev shell on aarch64-darwin, so scripts/build-once.sh:45 sources .direnv/flake-profile-cf2df07c….rc (2026-08-27), which prepends /nix/store/fi801q3i…-reprobuild-0.1.3/bin; build-once.sh:193 meanwhile resolves the ENGINE from the sibling checkout's build/bin before PATH, so the two disagree. bf_electron_write_stamp (ci/lib/build-freshness.sh:583) takes BF_BUILDER from `repro --version` off PATH.
new.suggestedRemedy: Have bf_electron_write_stamp take the builder from the `$repro_bin` build-once already resolved, and have build-once.sh say when it has sourced a dev-shell profile over an active one.
new.severity: P3 — provenance only; input_digest and artefact_sha256, the fields the gate compares, are unaffected.

new.title: the PLAT-37 Electron capture spec fails `the editor drew no rows` on frames whose editor the screen oracle can read
new.measured: 4 of 6 Playwright cases failed at plat37-electron-window-capture.spec.ts:862 at codetracer 596cb6e50. In three of them (editor, state, calltrace) the captured frame holds an editor pane the oracle located, with highlightedLineNumber 44 and 110 in two, and every route record is settled with the pinned final line. Either the DOM selector `div[id^='editorComponent'] .monaco-editor .view-lines .view-line` no longer matches what the product draws, or it is queried against the wrong page.
new.severity: P2 — it turns a real census finding into an opaque Playwright failure and makes the lane's exit code uninformative.

new.title: the GPUI freshness gate cannot see a stale isonim-gpui cdylib, and this pass found one
new.measured: The staged PLAT-37 shims were built 2026-10-16T12:35-12:37, two isonim-gpui commits behind the pinned 0317536 (2026-10-17T05:04) — commits that change font registration, line-height, per-corner radii and text antialiasing. `build-freshness.sh assert` returns 0 over that, by design (its own note, lines 114-116). The GPUI lane's two-polarity font_kit probe catches a shim with NO text, not a shim with the WRONG text metrics.
new.suggestedRemedy: Fold the staged shim's sha256 into the GPUI stamp with bf_digest_extra_file, or have the lane refuse a shim older than the pinned isonim-gpui revision.
new.severity: P2 — it is the exact contamination class the 2026-10-12 pass was invalidated by, one layer down.

new.title: `libs/nim-regex` is a submodule a scripted sync leaves uninitialised, and nothing builds without it
new.measured: At 596cb6e50 `git submodule status` printed `-a0f1df6a… libs/nim-regex` on a freshly synced checkout; `just build-gpui` died with `cannot open file: regex`. build-once.sh's preflight DOES name the cause (`MISSING 1 uninitialised submodule(s)`); the GPUI recipe does not.
new.severity: P3 — a workspace-sync gap; the remedy is one command.

new.title: reprobuild spends longer recording the portable fingerprint than running the build
new.measured: `just build-once` at codetracer 596cb6e50 with reprobuild build/bin/reprobuild (a192a91295-era): the 45-action graph reached `checked=43/45 running=0` and then spent ~43 further minutes single-threaded in recordPortableFingerprint -> portableAccessesOf -> isOwnOutput -> materialPath -> joinPathImpl, sampled twice six minutes apart in the same frame (28:56 CPU at 42:48 elapsed, RSS 1.87 GB). It did complete.
new.severity: P2 for anyone timing a build; belongs in reprobuild-pm, not codetracer-pm.
